results.title: Define with `threshold: {"floor": 0.4}`
results.evidence: accepted at definition and refused at evaluation ('no_reference'): `define` tests only that the threshold dict is non-empty, so a monitor written with the wrong vocabulary reads as active until somebody runs it — and the refusal lands on whoever is reading the monitor rather than whoever wrote it

results.title: Define two monitors with the same name on one model
Define with `escalate_after: -1`
results.evidence: `escalate_after: -1` was accepted and stored: nothing validates the field, and 0 already means *never escalate*, so a negative is a number with no reading that goes into the escalation arithmetic
